Thanks Rachel — quick technical/compliance summary below (high level + attachments). Happy to refine for legal wording.

1) In-region processing/storage:
- Hosted API (shared environment): we offer region-specific routing that pins inference and associated ephemeral caches to EU regions. However, backups and some control-plane metadata currently live in our global control plane (log indices and metadata are pseudonymized). For absolute in-region guarantee (including backups/control plane), Dedicated or Private deployment is required.

2) SCCs and transfers:
- We execute EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) as part of our Data Processing Addendum (DPA) for EU customers. SCCs are in place — see attached draft attestation and the signed DPA excerpt.
- Per Schrems II / EDPB guidance, SCCs reduce transfer risk but cannot eliminate it entirely when access by non-EU authorities is possible. We recommend a two-pronged approach: contractual (SCCs) + technical controls (encryption at rest with keys customer-controlled in-region, tight access controls, and logging).

3) Key management (KMS/HSM):
- For Private deployments: we can integrate with customer KMS (bring-your-own-key) fully located in the EU — customer retains key custody and we never export plaintext.
- For Dedicated on cloud: we can provision a dedicated KMS instance in EU cloud region; integration and rotation policies are configurable.

4) Deletion & evidence:
- We support tenant-scoped deletion APIs and configurable retention policies. For Dedicated/Private we can provide immutable audit logs and signed deletion attestations (PDF) with timestamped audit entries. For hosted customers we provide logs and deletion confirmations but not the same level of isolated immutable audit trail unless on Dedicated.

Attachments included: SCCs_Attestation_DRAFT.pdf, kms-eu-config-snippet.txt

Immediate asks from our side:
- Confirm whether MedTech requires backups & control-plane data to remain in EU (not just inference and data-at-rest).
- Confirm preference: Hosted+SCCs vs Dedicated vs Private (impacts timeline & cost).

Estimated time to produce a polished attestation for legal: 3 business days once we confirm the deployment option and the exact scope (inference+logs+backups).

Thanks everyone — adding the legal perspective (high level).

- Contractual posture: we can commit to SCCs (we use the latest EDPB-adopted text). We can sign an addendum that includes SCCs and Data Processing terms. However, per precedent and EDPB guidance, SCCs cannot be presented as an absolute guarantee against access by non-EU authorities. Our attestation should avoid absolute statements ("no transfers") and instead be scoped to what we actually control: routing, storage location, KMS custody, and deletion evidence.

- Recommended attestation language (draft bullet points):
  * Redwood Inference will process and store MedTech Systems tenant data in the EU region(s) as configured for the customer environment (inference, model cache, and customer data).
  * For Dedicated/Private deployments, backups and control-plane metadata for the customer will be stored in EU-only infrastructure and access to encryption keys can be retained by the customer (BYOK).
  * Redwood executes the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) as part of the DPA. SCCs are supplemented by technical measures (customer-controlled keys, encryption at rest/in transit, access logging).
  * While our technical and contractual measures materially reduce transfer risk, no provider can eliminate legal regimes that may require disclosure under foreign laws; this is a legal risk that SCCs and technical measures mitigate but do not fully remove.

- Action items:
  1) Rachel/Ben: confirm MedTech's preferred deployment and whether backups/control-plane indicators must remain EU-only.
  2) Neha: finalize the two-page attestation PDF reflecting the bullets above, attach the DPA excerpt and KMS configuration note.
  3) I will review and propose final legal-safe phrasing for sign-off.

Markus suggested times for a short legal call with MedTech legal this week. MedTech legal: are you available tomorrow at 11:00 CEST for a 30-minute call?

Best regards,
